newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Volatility deals struck as UK shares fall.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Volatility deals struck as UK shares fall.

text.p: Volatility trades involving FTSE 100 index options were the main deals struck on Friday in the UK equity options market as share prices fell sharply, dealers said.
One such deal was from a seller of 1,000 February 4350 calls at 17p who hedged this long position by buying March FTSE futures at 4244.
If the deal was properly hedged then if the market goes up the gains from the long futures will be offset by losses from the short options and vice versa if the market falls.
The deal will be profitable if market volatility decreases.
Another trader taking the view that volatility will increase bought 1,000 March 4100 puts at 50p against selling March futures at 4226.

The purchase of out-of-the-money puts was favoured by one trader who bought 400 February 4000 puts at 9p. Dealers believe this may have been to protect a share portfolio from any further fall in stock prices.
This is because in general, the puts should gain in value if share prices -- and therefore the portfolio -- fall. But if shares rise, the most that will be lost is the 9p option premium.
By 1503 GMT, spot FTSE was down 42.3 at 4229.2 and March futures had fallen 47 points to 4231.
Over in stock options, a tumble in oil shares prompted one trader to sell 640 April 600 calls at 126p and 127p in British Petroleum.
There was also a seller of 500 April 1050 calls at 42p in Shell Transport & Trading.
BP shares fell 12p to 724-1/2p while those of Shell were down 9-1/2p to 1054p.
